shots.title: Short-circuit sprint reset help before clearing state (#501)
shots.notes: Verified the existing sprint reset handler returns help before resetCommand and retagged the regression coverage to #501.

shots.title: Audit destructive subcommands for help-before-action handling (#501)

hazards.description: The audit found sibling nested-help hazards in session, worktree, and version release commands; all stayed within #501's requested destructive command audit.

shots.notes: Moved session help ahead of store-backed actions, guarded worktree start/cleanup/status dispatch with a help flag, and prevented version bump from entering release automation on nested help.

shots.title: Add CLI help safety regressions for destructive commands (#501)
shots.notes: Added regressions proving session start help does not register sessions, session prune help does not prune stale sessions, worktree start/cleanup help does not run git, version bump help does not enter release automation, and sprint reset help preserves state.

conditions.description: The Windows full test suite still emits legacy temp-repo stderr noise, but it passed and did not affect S138 validation.
Parallelizing `slope sprint gate` writes produced confusing intermediate gate messages; final state was intact, but SLOPE state mutations should be run sequentially.

training.description: Nested help must be routed before subcommand dispatch when the subcommand can mutate state.
training.outcome: Session, worktree, and version commands now check help before store, git, or release side effects.

nutrition.description: `corepack pnpm vitest run tests/cli/sprint-workflow.test.ts tests/cli/commands/session.test.ts tests/cli/commands/worktree.test.ts tests/cli/version.test.ts` passed: 43 tests.
`corepack pnpm typecheck`, `corepack pnpm prepare`, and `corepack pnpm test` passed on Windows: 228 test files passed, 1 skipped; 3601 tests passed, 25 skipped.
`slope roadmap validate` passed with existing historical roadmap warnings.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: Tight and trust-restoring. The original reset path was already repaired, and the audit turned up the real value: similar nested help hazards in adjacent stateful commands.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: For every stateful CLI family, route `--help` before resolving stores, checking git worktrees, invoking release automation, or parsing action flags.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The broadest risk was not `sprint reset` anymore; it was `session start --help`, `session prune --help`, and `worktree cleanup --all --help` slipping through subcommand dispatch.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: S139 can build on a cleaner trust baseline for guard recovery guidance.

bunker_locations: Nested help flags must bypass mutating subcommand handlers, even when action flags are present.
Destructive command audits should include release automation, worktree cleanup, and session cleanup paths, not just obvious reset commands.
Do not parallelize SLOPE commands that write the same sprint-state file.
yardage_book_updates: Session command help is now read-only for nested subcommands including start and prune.
Worktree command help is now read-only for nested start, cleanup, status, and list dispatch.
Version bump help no longer enters release automation.
Sprint reset, session, worktree, and version destructive-help regressions are covered by CLI tests and built CLI smoke.
course_management_notes: Validation passed: `corepack pnpm typecheck`, `corepack pnpm prepare`, `corepack pnpm test`, `slope roadmap validate`, and compiled CLI smoke.
Issue #501 should close when the PR containing S138 merges.
